projects.allunan:
Allunan™ is a creative studio that needed a portfolio able to win clients, not only display work. I designed the site and helped build it.

The site pairs a clean, simple layout with a touch of 3D and subtle animations. It gives visitors a feel for the studio's taste without getting in the way of the work. Before launch the studio had no inbound requests. Within two months, 15 came in.
projects.cineway:
A Moroccan video production agency came to us with a website that undersold their work. I designed a replacement that does it justice.

The new dark-mode portfolio puts their films first and lets their expertise speak through them. Now when they sit down with prospective clients, the site backs up the pitch, and the first impressions have been better. The client loved the result and praised the work.
projects.ceinty:
Running a short-term rental in Morocco means juggling bookings, guests and everything between. Ceinty is a new platform built to take that off a host's hands, and it needed a landing page to say so clearly.

I built that page to make a young product feel established and trustworthy from the first scroll. The client said the result "exceeded our expectations."
projects.geofile:
GeoFile is an analytics practice for leaders shaping the future of mineral investment, and it needed a brand that looks as rigorous as its work. I designed a full visual identity built on one idea: progress begins with understanding the ground beneath.

The mark is a mine seen from an angle, drawn like a topographic map. An earthy palette of ochre, sand and deep brown carries it across everything from social stories to caps. The new brand embodies the values and core of the company.
projects.haial:
Buying fine jewelry online asks a lot of trust. Haial, a high-end custom jewelry maker, needed a store that feels as considered as the pieces it sells.

Working with the Allunan™ team, I built an online store around large lifestyle images, so each piece is seen as it's worn, not just displayed. A restrained palette of pure blue and white keeps the focus on the jewelry and gives the store a quiet, premium feel.
projects.volta:
Charging an EV should feel as simple as filling a tank, and Volta wants to make it so. As an EV charging network for drivers and businesses, it needed a landing page that makes that promise at a glance.

I built the page around the two audiences it serves: a clear path for drivers to find, reserve and pay, and an invitation for businesses to join the partner program and host fast chargers.
projects.ormeo:
Accounting is a business of trust, and trust starts with the first impression. Ormeo Experts Comptables, an accounting and financial advisory firm, wanted a website that looked as reliable as the work they do.

Working with the Allunan™ team, I redesigned their website to modernize their digital presence while keeping their existing brand identity. The new site presents the firm the way it works: clear, precise and dependable, with its expertise front and centre and its values clear in every detail.

experiments.synthetictheatre:
Some websites are worth taking apart to see how they work. synthetictheatre.com is one of them, so I rebuilt it from scratch as a personal exercise in Next.js, React and GSAP.

Credits go to Daniele Buffa, Andreas Antonsson, and everyone who helped make this masterpiece.
experiments.emmaissocial:
Great websites reward a closer look, and emmaissocial.com is one I kept coming back to. I rebuilt it from scratch as a personal exercise in Next.js, React and GSAP, to see how it's put together.

Credits go to DashDigital, Salt and Pepper, and everyone who helped make this masterpiece.
experiments.metalab:
metalab.com is the kind of site other designers measure themselves against. I rebuilt it from scratch, as a personal exercise in Next.js, React and GSAP, to understand what makes it work.

Credits go to the MetaLab team, and everyone who helped make this masterpiece.
experiments.windows98:
Remember the sound of a Windows 98 startup? I rebuilt the desktop in the browser, so anyone can sit down at it again, no old computer needed.

It's a personal project built in Next.js, to see how much of an old operating system's character a website can carry.
experiments.nanocopy:
Good microcopy is easy to underrate and hard to write on a deadline. Nano Copy® is a collection of ready-to-use titles, slogans and short lines, in English, Arabic and German, that you can copy in one click.

It's inspired by microcopy.me, which shows how better headlines, CTAs and error messages improve the user experience.
experiments.finwind:
Finance is easier to trust when it's easier to understand. Finwind is a fintech company that wants to make banking simple and open to everyone, and its identity had to say that in one glance.

The logo is four fans, one for each cornerstone of financial prosperity: saving, investing, borrowing and protecting. Together they suggest momentum, a push toward what customers want to achieve.
experiments.mystic:
An identity for a digital-first creative studio that crafts mystical ideas and captivating visuals, helping ambitious brands rise above the digital noise.

At its heart is a star built from the golden ratio, a mark for harmony and visionary leadership. It opens a window onto the endless possibilities of space, where mystery meets innovation. A palette of lavender, purple and deep blue on near-black gives it a calm, confident tone.
